value: PRI01/1 connects owners that are already proven locally (MEM raw record and source-stop, TSK create/ask/answer/change/control, ART/VER/readback) to an ordinary sentence. With the refinements below, the first mock flow becomes: request, then same-Goal ask, answer or change, then saved draft, check, readback and source-stop. A natural turn drives it, and structured controls stay immediate. This materially improves on the rejected draft-only candidate and makes the single later authentic usefulness judgment meaningful. It is connection design only. It proves no usefulness, real-provider behavior, recovery, or product or P001 acceptance.
responsibilities: PRI owns only its own tables. These hold: the closed submit/get_turn wire; a turn ledger with UNIQUE(session_id,client_key) storing turn_id, the MEM record_ref and the MEM-stored hash (never raw text); a primary call ledger (admitted|returned|raised|not_entered|interrupted), which acts as the C15 role=primary record; snapshot metadata (disclosed refs and hashes, candidate fingerprint, exposure set, truncation); the closed proposal parser; an applying intent (exact normalized owner request, trusted request_scope, effect key); the final receipt and reply; one C14 event per terminal turn; startup turn reconciliation; and the structured-control endpoint. MEM owns sanitize-before-persist, the original record, C11 gating, stop_reference and its replay. TSK owns: source-safe C02 listing; Goal/Condition/event ID minting; grant intersection; revision, question and state checks; all budget reservation, including a new workless primary path against a finite shared host ceiling; and create/control receipts. The trusted host owns: request_scope and the host Grant ceiling; the RECOVERY01 guard and its phases; connection serialization; and sequencing of register, recover and finish_startup. The model returns only a reply plus one closed proposal that selects disclosed identifiers. It never mints IDs, grants, question IDs, conditions or completion. VER/complete stays outside PRI.
contract_alignment: C01: aligned once identity is defined as the sanitized input. MEM.append replays by client_key and compares sanitized text, so two raw inputs that sanitize identically return the same turn. This is acceptable and must be documented; raw text is never stored to tell them apart. Namespace the MEM key as dumps(['PRI01.append',session_id,client_key]), because MEM keys are global and include session only in the canonical input. Order: MEM.append (idempotent), then a short PRI insert of the turn. A crash between the two leaves a history-only record, and a resend completes it. C02: no listing exists, and get_work exposes brief and question text with no source gate, so a TSK addition is required (F2). C03: create already checks replay before grant and source checks, and minting is host-side. Replay canonical includes request_scope, so PRI must persist the exact scope it used. C04: questions come only from RUN/TSK. C05: append, read(model_context), search and stop_reference are usable. Remember/correct are deferred. C10: _answer/_change/control check revision without epoch and enforce question status and grant intersection. change rejects a reused origin, which matches one effect per turn. C14: owners already emit accepted/state events, so PRI adds only its own turn event (F9). C15: blocked by reserve_budget, which rejects workless calls and non-expert roles, and by MockInvoker, which is lease-bound (F4). RECOVERY01: guardless or legacy stores must not reserve workless model budget against an enrolled DB, so Primary execution needs the ready guard and waits on RECOVERY01 integration. Unsupported continue/attach/remember/correct proposals return visible invalid_input/unavailable and never degrade to none or new_work.
evidence_limits: Read only the listed files. TSK knowledge comes from the verbatim excerpts. The following are not inspected and are not claimed: _transaction replay ordering and failure storage; _current revision rejection; _reserve and any host-wide counter; the TaskStore override of invalidate_by_refs (the intake base refuses non-queued work); ask dependency capture; source-stop question closure; and MockInvoker. Statements about them are prerequisites, not facts. No tests run, no input or source hashes computed, no recovery or startup behavior observed, no provider call, no usefulness evidence. RECOVERY01 code and tests are pending and are not claimed to pass. Snapshot binding and verifier shape checks are host-side and do not adopt PRI01.
findings:
F1 Workless budget prerequisite. reserve_budget rejects a missing work_ref and any model role other than expert. Add a TSK path with kind=model, role=primary and no work_ref. It must: require an enrolled ready guard; charge only a finite shared host model ceiling that is required configuration (the excerpts show no host-wide counter, so TSK must own one); create no lease or Goal; replay by key; and allow consume to bind once to the PRI call_id with no refund on failure. Never fabricate a Goal or lease, and never use MockInvoker for conversation.
F2 Source-safe C02 listing prerequisite. Add TSK.list_candidates{session_id,limit<=20,goal_ids?}, read-only in one read transaction. It returns the latest non-superseded revision per Goal (terminal Goals included, for status questions), ordered by recent activity, with truncated:bool. Each item has: work_ref; state; brief_summary (purpose only, byte-bounded); open_questions{id,revision,text}; dependency_refs (registered sources plus question dependencies); and text_withheld:bool. Gate summary and question text through source_gate on those dependencies. Any stopped or unavailable dependency withholds the text but keeps the ID and state visible, so controls and ambiguity stay possible without leaking stopped content. PRI must never call get_work or SQL to obtain model-visible text.
F3 Fingerprint. Hash the ordered disclosed tuple (goal_id, revision, open question ids, text_withheld) plus truncated. Exclude epoch and state: claims move epoch constantly, C10 ignores epoch, and the owner transaction rechecks state. Recompare after the call returns and again immediately before dispatch. On mismatch, save a stale outcome with no effect, no re-inference and no proposal rewrite, show it visibly, and let a new turn decide. This check is best-effort and not atomic. Owner transactions remain the authority for revision, question and state. Membership is exposure, not semantic proof.
F4 Wrong-but-listed targets. Require: target work_ref and question_id came from the snapshot with the exact revision; answer.record_ref and change.origin_record_ref equal the turn record, otherwise reject (do not substitute); stop targets are disclosed same-session record refs. Never pick the latest Goal, use ordinals or fall back to a guess. Residual risk: a semantically wrong but listed pause/cancel/change still commits, and cancel is terminal. Mitigate with host receipts that name the target from owner data (goal purpose or state, never model text) and with immediate structured controls. Tests must cover wrong-but-listed cancel and answer.
F5 Provenance closure. Omitted dependencies are the real leak, because brief text may encode content from a disclosed record or candidate the model did not cite. For new_work and change, the host sets context_refs to the model-selected refs plus the turn record plus every disclosed model_context record plus the dependency_refs of disclosed candidates, deduplicated and bounded. The owner gate then makes source adoption atomic, and a later stop invalidates correctly. This over-invalidates by design, which is acceptable. A stop after exposure but before dispatch is rejected by the owner gate. answer is protected by the existing question-dependency and answer-record gate. pause/resume/cancel consume no content and are not gated.
F6 Grant. new_work uses create with the trusted fixed request_scope, intersected with the host Grant. change keeps the prior grant intersected with the host Grant. Model grant, capability, approval or cost fields fail parsing. Persist the scope in the applying intent, because a configuration change would otherwise make replay conflict.
F7 Commit gap. Persist the applying intent before dispatch. The effect key is dumps(['PRI01.effect',turn_id,kind]); stop uses its own MEM namespace. Live retry re-dispatches the identical request. Existing replay-first behavior returns the original receipt, which is verified for create and MEM and is a prerequisite for control. Failures are not replay-stored, so PRI saves the owner failure itself. Startup needs read-only TSK.get_create_by_key, TSK.get_control_by_key and MEM.get_stop_reference_by_key({key}), returning the original receipt or not_found. Under the held RECOVERY01 lock, local SQLite owner effects are atomic and synchronous, so not_found after the prior process ends decisively means never committed. Mark the turn interrupted and do not apply it.
F8 Transactions. MEM, create and control require an idle connection, so dispatch is never nested under a PRI BEGIN, and the model is never awaited inside a transaction. Given F5, no new atomic adoption seam is needed for the first slice. An owner on_commit hook stays a later option, not a prerequisite.
F9 C14. MEM.append and owner effects already emit events, so PRI must not duplicate state or work events. PRI writes one event per terminal turn through append_event with key dumps(['PRI01.turn',turn_id]), kind result or error, refs = turn record plus effect refs. Omit work_ref, because append_event rejects an epoch-moved work_ref as stale. Write it in the same short PRI transaction as the receipt. If the effect is rejected or uncommitted, suppress the model reply and show the host error, per D-029.
F10 Reply laundering. Do not append Primary replies as MEM assistant records in this slice. Do not feed C14 or turn replies back as model context. They may carry stopped-source content without tracked provenance. Context = turn record + bounded same-session usable records. Freeze an explicit recent-record listing rather than relying on the empty-query instr behavior of search.
F11 Lifetime. Hold guard.activity() from admission through callback end and saving the ending, including BaseException paths. Add PRI.recover_turns, called by the host in the startup phase after TSK recover and before finish_startup. It converts pending, admitted and returned-unadopted turns to interrupted, reconciles applying turns per F7, and never re-invokes for the same client_key.
F12 Structured controls. Separate closed endpoint {client_key,session_id,work_ref,command in pause|resume|cancel} plus record stop. Key dumps(['PRI01.control',session_id,client_key]). No model call, no Primary mutex, and no MEM record required. Only a short guard.operation permit plus serialized connection use, so controls never wait on a running callback.
recommendation:
REFINE, then adopt as PRI01/1. Sequencing:
(1) Root freezes the PRI01/1 doc: wire shapes and bounds, the closed proposal grammar (none|new_work|answer|control pause/resume/cancel/change|memory stop_reference only), the F3 fingerprint, the F4 target rules, the F5 provenance union, the F9 event and reply-suppression rules, the F10 context rule and F11 statuses.
(2) Fixed tests first. Then small additive owner changes from separate owners: TSK.list_candidates (F2); TSK workless primary reservation with a host ceiling plus consume (F1); TSK.get_create_by_key/get_control_by_key; MEM.get_stop_reference_by_key. All read-only except the reservation. No migration, no change to the lease table, no second engine.
(3) PRI module using only public owner calls. Temporary SQLite plus labeled mock callbacks. Cover: concurrent duplicate submit; key-input conflict; no transaction during the callback; reply-loss and restart without re-inference; malformed, extra, out-of-set and wrong-but-listed proposals; stopped original, context or candidate text before entry and before adoption; fingerprint, revision and question races; exact answer/change provenance; no grant enlargement; commit-gap lookup; immediate cancel while the callback is held; no complete; readback with no duplicate events.
(4) Host wiring only after RECOVERY01 and the following ART adoption are integrated. Primary requires the ready guard.
(5) Run the integrated mock flow demo.
(6) A separately frozen, finite real-provider proof under existing no-extra-charge access.
(7) The one authentic owner usefulness evaluation. That is the only human boundary, and it is already known. All other choices stay autonomous. Continue/attach and remember/correct remain deferred.
